stem.text: A building draws electrical power at a rate of W(t) kilowatts, where W is differentiable and t is measured in hours. Measured values are W(0) = 3, W(4) = 5, W(6) = 8, W(12) = 4. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{12} W(t)\,dt \), the energy, in kilowatt hours, used from t = 0 to t = 12, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 4 \cdot \frac{3 + 5}{2} = 16 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{5 + 8}{2} = 13 \); \( 6 \cdot \frac{8 + 4}{2} = 36 \).

distractor_derivations.B: trapezoidal sum with the common width (b - a)/3 used for every subinterval
distractor_derivations.C: factor 1/2 applied to the last trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.D: right Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
